key_insight: A modular system combines musical activity, visible instruments, image sharpness, and beat timing to choose concert camera views. Its interpretable scoring makes editing decisions traceable, though the supplied abstract reports mixed exploratory findings rather than clear performance gains.
problem_solved: Editing multi-camera concerts requires selecting visually clear, musically relevant shots while timing cuts to the performance.
method: Extract instrument activity from multitrack audio and assess visible instruments and image sharpness in each camera view.
Use beat-based timing to organize cuts and score camera views over complete shot intervals.
Select cameras probabilistically, then evaluate components and conduct an exploratory expert study on a four-camera concert.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the framework illustrates interpretable fusion of audio and visual signals for automated editing. The exploratory evidence does not establish consistent editing-quality improvements.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multitrack audio and camera feeds → feature extraction → scoring → camera selection.
Beat-aligned timeline showing instrument activity, shot intervals, and camera changes.
Four-camera grid annotated with visible instruments and image sharpness.
Score breakdown illustrating how musical relevance and visual quality contribute to view selection.
paper_title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
paper_authors: Lennart Schiweck, Adrian Kempf, Michelle Retig, Moritz Feucht, Tim Mangliers
